targets.summary: Tier loop reads tiers[i + 1] without bounding i, so the last tier dereferences undefined.
Balance is read before the awaits and written back after, so concurrent ticks lose updates.
await inside forEach is not awaited, so reserve() returns before any stock is decremented.
Loop bound is <= days, so every window contains one extra day.
discount is optional on the row but dereferenced unguarded, throwing for carts with no coupon.
The final attempt's rejection is swallowed, so retry resolves undefined instead of throwing.
settledAt is a nullable TypeORM column, so an unsettled row loads as null rather than undefined, and isSettled() returns true for every unsettled invoice.
The sweep interval started in the constructor is never cleared on destroy, so the timer keeps the process alive after shutdown.
eligible() returns the inactive suppliers, the exact opposite of what its documentation and name promise. No exception is thrown; the caller sends purchase orders to suspended suppliers.
discount is declared optional on CartRow and dereferenced without a guard, while the equally optional lines is guarded one line above.
The loop bound is <= lastPage, so pageBounds returns one more page than the documented ceil(total / pageSize), and the extra page is empty.
modifiedSince filters on createdAt instead of updatedAt, so an incremental sync silently skips every record that was edited after it was created.
Row permits an absent discount, which is dereferenced without a guard.

verdicts.reason: In priceLine, when line.quantity reaches or exceeds the last tier's minQuantity, `next` (tiers[i+1]) is undefined, so `next.minQuantity` throws a TypeError instead of selecting that top tier.

reserve() calls lines.forEach with an async callback that is never awaited; the function returns `{ orderId, reserved }` before any decrement/push has run, so `reserved` is always empty and stock decrements race unchecked.
windowDays loops `i <= days`, producing days+1 dates including start+days itself; for an 'inclusive-start, exclusive-end' window of `days` length this wrongly includes the exclusive boundary date.
`row.discount.amount` is read unguarded (unlike `row.lines || []`); calling cartTotals on a cart with no discount (e.g. {lines:[...]}) throws TypeError instead of treating discount as 0.
When every attempt throws, the loop ends without returning/throwing, so retry() resolves to undefined instead of rejecting with the last error, silently masking failures.

isSettled() checks `this.settledAt !== undefined`, but per the nullable-column contract (see receipt.entity.ts) an unset settledAt arrives as null, not undefined, so isSettled() always returns true even for unsettled invoices.
The setInterval sweep timer started in the constructor is never cleared in onModuleDestroy (only the entries map is cleared), leaking the interval/timer after the module is destroyed.
eligible() filters `!supplier.active`, returning suspended (inactive) suppliers, the opposite of the documented contract that active===false suppliers must never appear in the list.
CartRow.discount is typed optional, but `row.discount.amount` is accessed without a guard, throwing at runtime for any cart without a discount.

Loop uses `page <= lastPage` where lastPage=Math.ceil(total/pageSize), producing lastPage+1 entries (one extra out-of-range page with from===to===total) instead of the documented exactly-ceil(total/pageSize) entries.
modifiedSince is documented to return records changed after `since`, but filters on `createdAt`, so a customer edited after `since` whose record was created earlier is never returned.
Row.discount is optional (contracts.ts), but `row.discount.amount` is accessed unguarded, throwing TypeError for a row with no discount.

verdicts.reason: On the last tier iteration, next = tiers[i+1] is undefined, so next.minQuantity throws whenever line.quantity falls in or above the top tier.

markSeen stores Date.now() as the new watermark instead of the time settledSince was queried, so any payment that settles during the awaited ledger.write/markSeen calls falls before the new lastSeenAt and is permanently skipped by future settledSince queries.

reserve() uses lines.forEach with an async callback, so the reservation writes are never awaited and the function returns { orderId, reserved } before any decrements complete or reserved is populated.

`row.discount.amount` is accessed unconditionally (lines are defensively defaulted with `|| []` but discount isn't), so a cart row with no discount (undefined) throws a TypeError.

onModuleDestroy() clears the map but never calls `clearInterval(this.sweep)`; the background sweep timer keeps firing indefinitely after the module is destroyed, leaking the timer/keeping the process alive.
eligible() filters with `!supplier.active`, returning suspended suppliers instead of active ones — the inverse of the documented contract that suspended suppliers must never appear in the list.

modifiedSince filters by `row.createdAt > since` instead of an update/modified timestamp, so customers whose existing records were edited (not newly created) after `since` are omitted from incremental sync, contradicting the documented 'data changed' semantics.

verdicts.reason: For the last tier in the array, next is tiers[i+1]=undefined, so if line.quantity >= tier.minQuantity (the normal top-tier case), next.minQuantity throws a TypeError.

tick() reads balanceOf(account.id), awaits multiple I/O calls, then writes ledger.write(account.id, adjusted) computed from that stale balance; a concurrent write to the same account in between is overwritten with the stale-derived value.
reserve() uses lines.forEach with an async callback that is never awaited, so the function returns { orderId, reserved: [] } before any reservation completes, always reporting an empty reserved list.
Loop condition `i <= days` produces days+1 entries, contradicting the documented exclusive-end window and returning one extra date.
row.discount is accessed without a fallback, so a cart row with no discount (discount undefined) throws on row.discount.amount.
When all attempts fail, the catch block swallows the final error and the loop exits, causing retry() to resolve with undefined instead of throwing/rejecting.
settledAt is a nullable DB column so an unset value loads as null, but isSettled() only checks !== undefined, so unsettled invoices report true.
onModuleDestroy clears entries but never calls clearInterval on this.sweep, so the setInterval timer keeps firing and referencing the destroyed service after teardown (resource leak).
eligible() filters for !supplier.active, inverting the documented contract, so it returns only suspended suppliers instead of active ones.
row.discount is optional but accessed without a guard, so cartTotals throws when a cart row has no discount.
Loop condition `page <= lastPage` produces lastPage+1 entries (an extra empty page), violating the documented ceil(total/pageSize) count.
modifiedSince is documented to return records edited since the timestamp but filters on row.createdAt, so edited-but-not-newly-created rows are omitted and merely-created rows are wrongly included.
Row.discount is typed optional but discount() dereferences row.discount.amount without a guard, throwing when discount is undefined.
